title: Direct image compositor respects strict scalar extension
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, an algebra map $i:E\to F$, and their integer rings $A,B$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the derived categories of strict constant-coefficient module towers, the functors $G_H,J_H,R_H$, and their specified compositors [def-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-arrows], [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations], [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Let $T_W$ be finite scalar extension, $h_f$ the inverse of strictScalarPull, $b_f$ the openTensor map, and $a_f$ the proper scalar mate [def-pur-constant-scalar-tower-mates], [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate]. For arbitrary scheme maps $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ and $M\in D(\mathrm{Tow}(A_X))$, $T_Z(rComp_A);a_{gf}=a_gR_{f,A};R_{g,B}(a_f);rComp_B$. The comparison uses exactly the geometric direct-image compositors defined as conjugates of gComp.

proof.text: Compute the geometric transpose of the successive proper scalar maps by naturality of the first counit, strictProper_geometric_transpose for each factor, and naturality of the second scalar pullback comparison. It is the successive inverse pullback comparison followed by scalar extension of the composite counit.

Apply the generic scalar cube mate equation to gComp over A and B, with identity outer functors and the composite geometric adjunctions. Its left cube is strictScalarPullComposition. Its right mate is the desired direct-image scalar square, since rComp is the conjugate of gComp. Cancel the identity maps. This is a complete categorical proof from the pullback compositor equation.

theorem strictScalarProperComposition {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (M : Derived (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)) X) :
    (T l E F i Z).map
        ((rComp (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)) f g).hom.app M) ≫
        (proper l E F i (f ≫ g)).app M =
      (proper l E F i g).app
          ((R (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)) f).obj M) ≫
        (R (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l F)) g).map
          ((proper l E F i f).app M) ≫
        (rComp (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l F)) f g).hom.app
          ((T l E F i X).obj M)
lean.note: The section parameters l, E, F, i and their instances occur above the theorem in the module; this field reproduces its written signature verbatim.
